To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the participants (a) viewed accountability and democracy as conflicting concepts, but (b) believed that they should be reconciled in order to promote social justice.

(a) educational leaders can be prepared to be democratically accountable leaders by being taught to understand the relationship between democratic principles and accountability, (b) the relationship between democratic leadership and accountability is complex and multifaceted, and (c) democratic leadership and accountability are not mutually exclusive.

(1) the majority of participants were able to identify and link the principles of accountability and democracy; (2) the participants were able to link these principles with social justice; (3) the participants identified tensions and overlaps between the principles; and (4) the participants were unable to identify a single definition of social justice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How can we better prepare educational leaders to deal with conflicting concepts of democracy and accountability?
how the principles of democracy, social justice, and accountability can be used to create a more just society.
the ways in which educational leaders understand the concepts of democracy and accountability, and how they might be reconciled in the context of social justice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
democratic leadership is the only way to achieve social justice and that accountability should be viewed as a democratic process, not a top-down, punitive process.
democratically accountable leadership is a process of leadership, not an outcome.
the future of education is dependent on educational leadership.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the democratic principles of equality, freedom, and participation can be used as the basis for accountability in education.
we have found a way to reconcile these two seemingly contradictory concepts of democracy and accountability through a process of social justice that is grounded in democratic principles.
we have attempted to demonstrate that democratic accountability is a viable concept for educational leadership.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of democratic accountability, when applied to the preparation of future leaders in education, can be a powerful tool for social justice.
educational leaders must be prepared to lead in ways that are both socially just and democratic.
democratic accountability can be achieved by focusing on the principles of justice, equity, and fairness.
